passage: Asked about the missing funds, the treasurer was economical with the truth.
focus: Recognize understatement for dishonesty; do not infer exactly what was concealed.

passage: She found the proposal wanting, but wanted time to revise it.
focus: Distinguish deficient wanting from wanted time in the same sentence.

passage: He kept his powder dry by the stove before loading the musket.
focus: Literal gunpowder; do not apply strategic-restraint idiom automatically.

passage: His politeness was a locked door. Every courteous answer left her no closer to the truth.
selection: His politeness was a locked door
focus: Novel metaphor absent from phrase dictionary; do not assert private intent as fact.

passage: Apparently the printer needs another subscription. What a time to be alive.
selection: What a time to be alive
targets: likely ironic dismay rather than literal celebration
focus: Contemporary irony; qualify the reading and avoid inventing subscription details.

passage: The board described the losses as a temporary headwind, though revenue had declined for three years.
targets: adversity metaphor and possibly minimizing language
focus: Contrast temporary with three-year decline; no invented fraud or financial causes.

passage: Please close the door and leave the keys on the shelf.
focus: No useful automatic highlights for fluent reader. Do not invent locking.
